oneLineDescription: A free, open-source computerized maintenance management system for managing work orders, preventive maintenance, assets, inventory, and facilities.

routes.description: Work order management — list, create, assign, and track maintenance tasks
Asset registry — track equipment, view maintenance history
Location hierarchy for organizing facilities and sites
Spare parts inventory tracking with stock levels
Meter readings for condition-based maintenance triggers
Work order analytics — status, aging, time & cost
General settings, feature toggles, and configuration
API keys, webhooks, and third-party connectors
CSV/Excel data import for work orders, assets, etc.
Public work request submission portal (QR code accessible)
Pricing page with plan comparison (home site)

brandVoice.tone: Direct, practical, and empowering — speaks to maintenance professionals who are frustrated with disorganization and want reliable, no-nonsense tools that just work. Slightly informal, uses second-person address, and emphasizes ease of use and efficiency gains.

entryPages.text: Pricing page with CTA to register

steps.text: Visitor lands on the registration page.
Fills in first name, last name, email, phone, company name, and password.
Accepts terms and conditions and clicks 'Create your account'.
Email verification page instructs user to check inbox.
User clicks verification link in email.
User arrives at the work orders dashboard (first entry).

risks.signal: Form-field interactions; field abandonment; dwell > 30s on registration form without submit
risks.label: Registration form feels too long (6 fields minimum)

risks.signal: Dwell on email-verification page > 60s; no redirect to dashboard
risks.label: Verification email not received or lost in spam

risks.signal: First app_home page load; no clicks within 15s; scroll without action
risks.label: Empty dashboard with demo data — no clear first action

interventions.content: You're almost there! Just a few more fields and your maintenance hub will be ready.
interventions.goal: Reduce perceived effort and encourage form completion

interventions.content: Your Atlas CMMS account is waiting — click here to verify your email and start managing your maintenance operations.
interventions.goal: Re-engage users who haven't completed email verification within 10 minutes

interventions.content: Start by creating your first Work Order — tap the '+' button or try importing your existing data from Settings > Imports.
interventions.goal: Spotlight the single most valuable next action from the empty state

steps.text: User navigates to the Work Orders page.
Clicks 'Create Work Order' button.
Fills in title, description, priority, assigns worker/team, selects asset and location.
Optionally attaches files, sets due date, adds checklist tasks.
Submits the new work order.

risks.signal: Dwell > 45s on work order form; repeated tab-switching between form fields and asset/location selectors
risks.label: Too many fields to fill for a quick work order

risks.signal: Error banner visible: 'The Work Order couldn't be created'
risks.label: API error on work order submission

interventions.content: Only Title is required — you can always add details later. Submit now and update when you have more info.
interventions.goal: Reduce friction by clarifying minimum viable input

interventions.content: That didn't go through. Check your network connection and try again — your form data is preserved.
interventions.goal: Prevent abandonment after a failed submission

steps.text: User navigates to the Preventive Maintenance section.
Clicks to create a new preventive maintenance schedule.
Configures trigger (time-based or meter-based), assigns asset, sets recurrence.
Assigns worker/team, attaches checklist.
Saves the preventive maintenance schedule.

steps.label: PM schedule active and generating work orders

risks.signal: Dwell > 60s on trigger configuration form; repeated back-button presses; tab-switching to docs
risks.label: Unclear how to configure frequency and trigger conditions

risks.signal: Error banner visible: 'The Work Order couldn't be scheduled'
risks.label: PM creation fails due to validation errors

interventions.content: Start simple: set a daily or weekly frequency. You can always refine the trigger later or switch to meter-based once readings are flowing.
interventions.goal: Unblock users stuck deciding on trigger configuration

interventions.content: Check that the trigger name and frequency are filled in — frequency must be at least 1 day.
interventions.goal: Surface the specific validation requirement blocking submission

steps.text: User navigates to the Imports section for assets.
Uploads a CSV/Excel file with asset data.
Maps columns to asset fields.
Reviews and confirms the import.

risks.signal: Repeated file upload attempts; error banners after upload; dwell > 30s without successful upload
risks.label: File format or column structure doesn't match expected template

risks.signal: Idle on column mapping screen > 45s; repeated field reassignments
risks.label: Unclear which CSV columns map to which asset fields

interventions.content: Download our template CSV from the import page to see the expected format. Your file just needs columns for Name, Location, and any custom fields you use.
interventions.goal: Provide the direct path to the correct file format

interventions.content: Only 'Asset Name' is required — unmatched columns can be skipped and added manually later.
interventions.goal: Reduce mapping anxiety by clarifying minimum required fields

entryPages.text: Public request portal accessible via QR code or URL

steps.text: Requester scans QR code or visits the public portal URL.
Fills in the request form describing the maintenance issue.
Submits the request.

steps.label: Request submitted and visible to maintenance team

risks.signal: Dwell > 30s on request form; no field interactions after page load
risks.label: Public requester unsure what to fill in or which fields are required

interventions.content: Just describe the problem in a sentence or two — the maintenance team will follow up if they need more details.
interventions.goal: Lower the perceived effort for non-technical requesters

steps.text: User encounters upgrade prompt or navigates to subscription plans.
Compares plan tiers and selects a higher plan.
Enters payment details via Paddle checkout.
Confirms the subscription upgrade.
Payment success confirmation page.

risks.signal: Dwell > 60s on plan comparison; repeated hover on different plans without selection; plan-modal interaction without confirm
risks.label: Decision fatigue between Starter, Professional, and Business tiers

risks.signal: Paddle checkout opened then abandoned; return-to-plans loop within same session
risks.label: User needs internal approval before committing payment

interventions.content: Based on your team size and current usage, Professional gives you advanced analytics and a customizable request portal — the features most teams upgrade for.
interventions.goal: Collapse the choice to a single recommended plan

interventions.content: Still deciding on your Atlas CMMS upgrade? Here's a one-page summary of what your team gains with the Professional plan — share it with your finance team.
interventions.goal: Enable the champion to defend the upgrade internally with a shareable asset

steps.text: Admin navigates to People & Teams.
Clicks 'Invite Users' button, opening the invite dialog.
Invite user dialog: admin enters email addresses and selects a role.
Submits the invitation.

risks.signal: Dwell > 30s on invite dialog; role selector opened and closed without confirm
risks.label: Admin unsure which role (Admin, Technical, Limited Technical) to assign

interventions.content: Most field technicians start as 'Technical' users — they can close work orders and log time. You can always change their role later.
interventions.goal: Remove role-selection paralysis with a sensible default recommendation

notes: Atlas CMMS is a monorepo with three packages: frontend (React SPA — the main CMMS app), home (Next.js marketing site), and mobile (React Native). The frontend uses Material UI 5, Redux Toolkit for state, react-router-dom 5/6 for routing, react-i18next with 18 language bundles, and Paddle for payments. Authentication is JWT-based with an OAuth2 callback route. The app supports white-labeling (custom logos, brand names via config). The marketing home site uses next-intl for i18n. The subscription has 4 tiers: Basic (free), Starter ($10/mo/user), Professional ($15), Business ($40). Self-hosted licensing is also available.
